extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy, law, and natural-law theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted normative rules and definitions from a political-philosophical treatise (Hobbes' Leviathan) concerning the laws of nature, justice, personhood, authority, and the formation of commonwealths. Focus is on the prescriptive standards and procedural rules the text advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothing Done To A Man, By His Own Consent Can Be Injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatsoever is done to a man, conformable to his own Will signified to the doer, is no Injury to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action is done with the person's expressed will and he has not previously surrendered the relevant right by covenant, it is not an injury. If he has surrendered the right, then his subsequent consent operates as a release of the covenant and likewise prevents it from being an injury. Implies attention to prior covenants and the scope of consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice Commutative, And Distributive
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice of Actions is divided into Commutative, and Distributive; the former consists in proportion arithmetical, the latter in proportion geometrical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commutative justice relates to equality of value in contracts (buying, selling, hiring, lending, exchanging) and is the justice of contractors (performance of covenant). Distributive justice (equity) is the justice of an arbitrator in defining what is just and distributing benefits according to merit; the text warns that 'merit' is not due by justice but is rewarded by grace, and that value in contracts is measured by the appetite of the contractors (consent determines just value).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Fourth Law Of Nature, Gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: "That a man which receiveth Benefit from another of meer Grace, Endeavour that he which giveth it, have no reasonable cause to repent him of his good will."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gratitude depends on antecedent free-gift; without it benevolence and mutual help collapse, leading to war. Ingratitude is a breach analogous to injustice against covenant. Emphasizes the social utility of gratitude for sustaining trust and peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Fifth, Mutuall accommodation, or Compleasance
rubrics_metrics.description: "That every man strive to accommodate himselfe to the rest."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained via an analogy to stones in building: selfish asperity or stubbornness that consumes more than one fills harms the social edifice. Observers of this law are 'sociable'; violators are cast out as troublesome. Frames mutual accommodation as required for peace and social survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sixth, Facility To Pardon
rubrics_metrics.description: "That upon caution of the Future time, a man ought to pardon the offences past of them that repenting, desire it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pardon is granting of peace; granting pardon to repentant parties (with security for the future) is required by the law of nature because refusing signals aversion to peace. Distinguishes between genuine peace and peace bought by fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Seventh, That In Revenges, Men Respect Onely The Future Good
rubrics_metrics.description: "That in Revenges ... Men look not at the greatnesse of the evill past, but the greatnesse of the good to follow."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment/revenge must be designed only for correction of the offender or deterrence of others (future good). Revenge aimed at triumph or glorying in hurt is vain, cruel, and tends to war; punishment without regard to future benefit is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Eighth, Against Contumely
rubrics_metrics.description: "That no man by deed, word, countenance, or gesture, declare Hatred, or Contempt of another."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because signs of hatred or contempt provoke fights (men often risk life to avenge honor), the law forbids expressions of contempt. The breach is called contumely; observance reduces provocations to violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Ninth, Against Pride
rubrics_metrics.description: "That every man acknowledge other for his Equall by Nature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects natural hierarchy as basis for domination; asserts equality by nature as necessary for entering peaceful conditions on equal terms. Pride (denying equality) undermines peace and is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Tenth Against Arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: "That at the entrance into conditions of Peace, no man require to reserve to himselfe any Right, which he is not content should be reserved to every one of the rest."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the formation of peace, one must not claim special rights one would deny others; modesty is required and pleonexia (desire of more than one's share) is condemned. Ties to the requirement of mutual concession when establishing commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Eleventh Equity
rubrics_metrics.description: "If a man be trusted to judge between man and man, that he deale Equally between them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge entrusted to decide must be impartial and give each his due; partiality (acceptance of persons) deters use of judges and tends toward war. Equity is presented as distributive justice; partiality is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Twelfth, Equall Use Of Things Common
rubrics_metrics.description: "That such things as cannot be divided, be enjoyed in Common, if it can be; and if the quantity of the thing permit, without Stint; otherwise Proportionably to the number of them that have Right."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where division is impossible, common enjoyment (or proportional sharing) is required to preserve equity; unequal distribution is contrary to equity and the law of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Thirteenth, Of Lot
rubrics_metrics.description: When things cannot be divided nor enjoyed in common, the law of nature requires that the entire right, or an alternation of use (first possession) be determined by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lot provides an impartial means to attain equal distribution where other means fail; presented as a legitimate method grounded in equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Fourteenth, Of Primogeniture, And First Seising
rubrics_metrics.description: Of lots there be two sorts, Arbitrary (agreed by competitors) and Naturall (either Primogeniture or First Seisure); things that cannot be enjoyed in common ought to be adjudged to the first possessor, and in some cases to the first-born.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes accepted customary rules (primogeniture) and first seizure as natural means of assignment; frames them as species of lot/assignment when division impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Fifteenth, Of Mediators
rubrics_metrics.description: "That all men that mediate Peace, be allowed safe Conduct."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intercession (mediation) is a means commanded by the law that aims at peace; mediators must be granted protection/safe conduct so they can perform the means necessary for peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sixteenth, Of Submission To Arbitrement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to a question should covenant mutually to stand to the sentence of another (an arbitrator) to avoid war; submission to arbitrament is thus of the law of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes questions of fact (was it done?) and right (was it unlawful?). Without agreement to accept an arbitrator's sentence, disputes remain unresolved and the condition of war persists.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Seventeenth, No Man Is His Own Judge
rubrics_metrics.description: No man is a fit arbitrator in his own cause; even if fit, equity requires equal admission of judges for each party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing one party to judge his own cause undermines equity and leaves controversies unresolved; impartial tribunals are required for peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Eighteenth, No Man To Be Judge, That Has In Him Cause Of Partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: No man in any cause ought to be received for Arbitrator, to whom greater profit, honour, or pleasure apparently ariseth out of the victory of one party, than of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apparent interest equates to a bribe (even if unavoidable); such partiality discredits the arbitrator and undermines trust—thus forbidden by the law of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Nineteenth, Of Witnesse
rubrics_metrics.description: In a controversie of Fact, where judge cannot give more credit to one party than the other, he must give credit to a third (or more) witness; otherwise the question is left to force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple impartial witnesses are required to resolve factual questions; reliance on force occurs if no adequate testimony is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Rule, By Which The Laws Of Nature May Easily Be Examined
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not that to another, which thou wouldest not have done to thy selfe."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The golden-rule test: weigh actions toward others by placing them in the other's position; if they seem too heavy for the other, then the action violates the laws of nature. Offers a simple method for moral assessment accessible to all capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Lawes Of Nature Oblige In Conscience Alwayes, But In Effect Then Onely When There Is Security
rubrics_metrics.description: The lawes of nature bind In Foro Interno (conscience) always; they bind In Foro Externo (action) only when there is security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If observance of the law externally would make one prey to others or cause self-ruin, external obedience is not required. Points to a tension between moral duty and self-preservation: obligations internal but conditional in practice by safety considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Laws Of Nature Are Eternal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lawes of Nature are Immutable and Eternall; injustice, ingratitude, arrogance, pride, iniquity, acception of persons, and the rest, can never be made lawfull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts permanence and universality of these moral precepts: certain vices cannot legitimately be legalized because they contradict preservation and peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: And Yet Easie
rubrics_metrics.description: These laws oblige only to a sincere and constant endeavour; therefore they are easy to be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One need only endeavour to perform them; continuous effort counts as fulfillment. Presents a lenient standard of moral performance (effort rather than perfect compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Science Of These Lawes, Is The True Morall Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The science of the laws of nature is the true and only moral philosophy: the study of what conduces to the conservation and defence of men in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts Hobbes' instrumentalist account of virtues (as means to peace) with other moralists who locate virtue in mediocrity of passions. Emphasizes practical, peace-oriented criterion for what is good.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Person What
rubrics_metrics.description: A PERSON is he whose words or actions are considered, either as his own, or as representing the words or actions of an other man, or of any other thing to whom they are attributed, whether Truly or by Fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines personhood in terms of consideration of actions/words as one's own or as representation. Introduces stage-derived language (persona/prosopon) and grounds for legal/representative roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person Naturall, And Artificiall
rubrics_metrics.description: When words/actions are considered as his own he is a Naturall Person; when considered as representing another he is a Feigned or Artificiall person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes natural persons from those acting in representative capacity (attorneys, deputies, actors). Relevant for attributing responsibility and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actor, Author; Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Of persons artificiall, some have their words and actions owned by those whom they represent: the Actor acts by Authority; he that owneth his words and actions is the AUTHOR; Authority is the right of doing any act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets terminology: author = one who owns actions; actor = representative; authority = right/commission. Important for allocating legal/political responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covenants By Authority, Bind The Author
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actor maketh a Covenant by Authority, he bindeth thereby the Author, no lesse than if he had made it himselfe; and no lesse subjecteth him to all the consequences of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covenants made within the scope of an actor's commission bind the principal (author). Caveat: actor binds author only within the commission's limits; contracting with an actor without knowing his authority is at one's own peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: But Not The Actor (When Acting By Author's Command Against Law)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actor doth any thing against the Law of Nature by command of the Author, if he be obliged by former Covenant to obey him, not he, but the Author breaketh the Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If obedience to an authority compels an actor to perform an act contrary to the law of nature, blame falls on the author who commanded it (refusal might itself breach covenant). Distinguishes responsibility between commander and commanded in constrained relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Authority Is To Be Shewne
rubrics_metrics.description: He that maketh a Covenant with the Author by mediation of the Actor, not knowing what Authority he hath, doth it at his own perill; if such Authority be not made manifest upon demand, the covenant is no longer obliged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making agreements through representatives, authority must be shown when demanded; otherwise the covenant may be invalid. If one expects only the actor's word as assurance, then the actor himself becomes the de facto author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Things Personated, Inanimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Inanimate things (church, hospital, bridge) may be personated by a rector, master, or overseer, but inanimate things cannot be Authors; actors may have authority given by owners or governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personation of inanimates requires an underlying civil state; cannot confer authorship to the inanimate object itself. Relevant to institutional representation and legal fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrational (Children, Fools, Mad-men) Personation
rubrics_metrics.description: Children, Fooles, and Mad-men that have no use of Reason, may be personated by Guardians or Curators; but can be no Authors during that time, longer than until they recover reason and judge the action reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians can give authority on behalf of irrational persons within a civil state; authorship may be retroactively accepted once reason recovers. Addresses capacity and representation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: False Gods
rubrics_metrics.description: An Idol or meer Figment may be personated by officers appointed by the State and held possessor of goods dedicated to them, but idols cannot be Authors; the authority proceeds from the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates that personation is a legal/state fiction: the state's appointment provides authority for cultic/personated entities, but no metaphysical authorship lies in the idol.

rubrics_metrics.name: The True God (Personation by Prophets, Christ, Holy Ghost)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true God may be personated: e.g., by Moses (governing Israelites in God's name), by Christ (sent from his Father), and by the Holy Ghost in the Apostles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides theological examples of personation where actors claim to speak in God's name; distinguishes divine personation from mere idols via claimed divine commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Multitude Of Men, How One Person
rubrics_metrics.description: A Multitude of men are made One Person when they are by one man or one Person Represented, so that it be done with the consent of every one of that Multitude in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity of the representer, not the represented, makes the common person; each member must consent individually for the representative to bear their person. Basis for formation of a commonwealth by mutual covenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every One Is Author (When Representative's Commission Limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The multitude naturally is many, not one; they are many Authors of every thing their Representative saith or doth in their name, each giving authority in particular; if they limit the representative, none owns more than the commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When people limit the representative's commission, they retain authorship for acts beyond that commission. Emphasizes the importance of understanding and delimiting representative authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: An Actor May Be Many Men Made One By Plurality Of Voyces
rubrics_metrics.description: If the representative consist of many men, the voyce of the greater number must be considered the voyce of them all; the unity is the voice of the greater number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majoritarian rule: the larger number's decision represents the whole. Highlights how assemblies translate plurality into a single representative act; raises issues for tied or parity cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives, When The Number Is Even, Unprofitable
rubrics_metrics.description: A Representative of even number, especially when the number is not great, whereby the contradictory voyces are oftentimes equall, is oftentimes mute and uncapable of Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evenly split votes lead to paralysis; examples include how not condemning amounts to absolving in certain contexts, and ties may operate as dilation instead of decisive action. Warns on assembly design to avoid deadlock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative Voyce (Veto by Single Member in Odd-numbered Assemblies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereof every one has by a Negative Voice authority to take away the effect of all the Affirmative Voices of the rest; in this number the assembly is no Representative, becoming oftentimes mute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If individual negative votes can nullify the rest (effective veto), the assembly fails as a representative body; composition and voting rules matter for representation efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors There Be Two Sorts (Simple and Conditional/Suretyes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors simply so called (own the action of another simply) and those who own conditionally (undertake to do it if the other doth not by a certain time), called suretyes, fidejussores, sponsores, praedes, vades, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes principal forms of authorship and suretyship (conditional principal liability). Relevant to obligations of sureties for debt, appearance, and other conditional commitments.
